messages:
Anya: Heads-up — CI eval run for the new quantized-ggml model leaked customer-like prompts into the artifacts bucket. Found unredacted prompts in the runner stdout tarball.

Cheng: Whoa, how did that happen? We have the redaction step in the artifact pipeline.

Anya: Looks like streaming path bypasses the `sanitize_for_artifacts` hook. When runner does chunked stream -> local buffer -> tar, it writes raw chunks before the final sanitizer callback.

Marco: Can you paste repro logs?

Anya: Sure — snip:
```
[2026-03-14T09:12:02Z] stream.recv: "user: My SSN is 123-45-6789, account 8675309"
[2026-03-14T09:12:02Z] runner.write_tmp: /tmp/eval/stream-abc.log
[2026-03-14T09:12:03Z] artifact.uploader: uploading /tmp/eval/stream-abc.log -> s3://eval-artifacts/ontop/1842345678/stream-abc.tar
```
Sanitizer only runs on final JSON blob; streaming buffer never passed through.

Priya: That's bad. Do we know scope of customers exposed? Prod run used anonymized synthetic prompts but some seeded customer-like strings slipped in via dataset fuzzing.

Tessa: Suggest immediate mitigation: 1) rotate access keys for the bucket; 2) revoke any short-lived tokens used by that job; 3) run a targeted scan on s3 prefix for PIIs (SSN, emails). I'll take ops actions.

Cheng: I can add an S3 lifecycle ACL to quarantine the prefix and restrict read to security team only. Also adding an S3 Object Lock won't help retroactively but can stop deletions.

Marco: Long-term fix: rearchitect streaming path so every chunk is sanitized at emit-time. Add `sanitize_chunk()` in the stream adapter and unit tests that assert no raw PII bytes reach disk. Also add a CI job that runs a synthetic prompt containing test markers (e.g., `<<PII-TEST:SSN=111-22-3333>>`) and fails if artifacts contain that pattern.

Anya: Agreed. We should also add a pre-upload hook in artifact-uploader that runs a lightweight regex redaction and a binary scan for known patterns.

Priya: Security additions:
- log an incident ticket with PII severity
- create short-lived tokens for eval jobs only (no long-lived credentials in runners)
- restrict artifact-bucket write-only to runner, read by ops through role-assume only

Tessa: I'll open the incident and attach the s3 object list. tagging @security @legal

eval-bot: CI job eval-runner/ontop (build #492) — status: failed — reason: artifact-scan detected `PII_TEST_TAG` in /tmp/eval/stream-abc.log

Cheng: Nice — that's the new upload-hook test I merged yesterday. It caught a repro in the staging pipeline. We should backport to master and deploy to prod CI tomorrow.

Marco: Metrics & observability todo:
- emit metric `eval.artifact.unredacted_count` with labels {env, run_id, model}
- dashboard: count by run -> heatmap of offending patterns
- alert: fire if unredacted_count > 0 in prod

Anya: Also add a privacy flag on eval runs: `--data-scope=private|synthetic|public`. If `private`, runner enforces double-scrub and pushes artifacts to isolated bucket with stricter ACLs.

Priya: For model onboarding security checklist: include a gate that validates streaming redaction, tokenization parity checks (so regex matches across token boundaries), and a manual sign-off from sec for any run that touches `private` data.

Tessa: I'll update the onboarding doc after incident ticket. For immediate rollout, plan:
1) Deploy chunk sanitizer to runner (Cheng + Marco)
2) Backport upload-hook to prod CI (Cheng)
3) Quarantine and scan bucket (Tessa)
4) Add dashboard + alert (Marco)
5) Add gating tests to onboarding pipeline (Priya)

Anya: Thanks all. Filing follow-ups in the incident — will paste ticket link when created.

Tessa: Incident created: INC-2026-032 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-032) — assigned to @Priya, @Cheng

Priya: Taking ownership. Will also add a retro note for the eval dashboard to show PII exposure timeline.

Marco: Quick question for CI wiring: should the upload-hook run inside job container (fast) or as a sidecar process that streams directly from tar stream (isolation)? I prefer sidecar for defense in depth.

Cheng: Sidecar wins for isolation, but make sure the sidecar doesn't inherit secrets. Use signed URLs with expire=60s and a short-lived token minted by the CI controller.

Anya: One more: add an integration test that fuzzes token boundaries (e.g., split `1-23-45` across chunks) — past regex-based redactors missed those.

eval-bot: Note: new PR merged — users/cheng/prompt-scrub-sidecar. CI run queued.

Marco: Good. Let's keep responses short in the incident channel; we'll run a blameless postmortem after containment.

Priya: Will draft remediation timeline and post to the ticket by EOD.

Anya: Closing loop: once fixes land, we should re-run the full eval-sanity-suite on all recent models to ensure no other artifacts contain tags.

Cheng: Acknowledged.
